findings.claim: process_events drops events that have distinct ids but share a kind, because deduplication keys on event["kind"] instead of event["id"].
evidence: lead probe: process_events([e(1,'created'), e(2,'created'), e(1,'created')]) -> handled ids [1]
test_events.py:13,18 give every distinct id its own kind, so `python3 -m unittest` passes (2 tests OK) while I1 is broken (merged from acceptance-3 and tests-1)
findings.failure_mechanism: two distinct events of the same kind (e.g. two 'created' events with ids 1 and 2) -> the second is skipped as if it were a redelivery -> a legitimate event is silently never handled, which breaks I1 and R1/A1; the tests cannot detect it

findings.claim: process_events drops events that have distinct ids but share a kind already handled.
findings.failure_mechanism: two distinct events with the same kind -> the second is skipped -> a distinct event is lost
findings.rejection_reason: Duplicate of the accepted root cause invariants-1 (dedup keyed on kind); merged.

findings.claim: A redelivered id is passed to the handler again when its kind has not been seen yet.
findings.failure_mechanism: same id arrives with a kind not seen yet -> the kind check passes -> the handler runs twice for that id
findings.severity_change_reason: Same root cause as invariants-1; the trigger falls outside the contract's notion of a redelivery.
findings.rejection_reason: The trigger needs a 'redelivery' with a different kind. The contract describes a redelivery as the same event repeated, so its kind matches and it is skipped (lead probe [1, 2]). The underlying wrong-key root cause is already accepted as invariants-1.

findings.claim: The test suite cannot tell deduplication by id from deduplication by kind, so it passes on the defective code.
evidence: test_events.py:13,18 use a distinct kind for every distinct id
findings.failure_mechanism: test data maps ids to kinds 1:1 -> kind-keyed and id-keyed dedup behave the same -> the defect goes undetected
findings.severity_change_reason: Test that cannot fail while its requirement is broken is merged into the code defect.
findings.rejection_reason: Under test-strength rules this is evidence of invariants-1, not a separate defect; merged into invariants-1.

findings.claim: No test covers distinct ids that share a kind; the suite passes although events.py deduplicates by kind instead of id.
evidence: test fixtures map id 1:1 to kind
findings.failure_mechanism: two events with distinct ids and the same kind -> the second never reaches the handler -> silent loss while the tests pass
findings.severity_change_reason: Merged into invariants-1 as its test evidence.
findings.rejection_reason: Duplicate symptom of the accepted root cause invariants-1 (a test that cannot fail while the requirement is broken is merged into the code defect).

findings.claim: Redelivery is suppressed only because it repeats the kind, not the id; the same id with a different kind is handled twice.
findings.failure_mechanism: same id with a different kind -> handled twice
findings.severity_change_reason: The input is outside the contract's data rules, and the root cause is already accepted.
findings.rejection_reason: The reviewer concedes this input cannot occur under the contract (a redelivery is the same event). Same root cause as invariants-1; merged.
